view.stem: 在本课研究的凸多面体中，面数最少的多面体是什么？它有多少条棱、多少个顶点和多少条多面体对角线？选择完整描述正确的一项。这里的对角线连接不在同一个面上的两个顶点。

options.text: 四面体；6条棱，4个顶点，3条对角线。
四面体；6条棱，4个顶点，0条对角线。
四面体；12条棱，4个顶点，0条对角线。
三棱柱；9条棱，6个顶点，0条对角线。

intent.task: Identify the convex polyhedron attaining the least face count, then determine its edge, vertex and spatial-diagonal counts under the lesson definition.
intent.source_solution: Each side of a convex face has a distinct neighboring face: two supporting face planes intersect on at most one line. Since a face has at least three sides, at least four faces are needed. A tetrahedron attains four faces, has four vertices and C(4,2)=6 edges. Every pair of vertices shares a face, so it has zero spatial diagonals. Regularity is neither assumed nor needed. The current 49-degree-shaped circle marker is copied untouched into the seed; its historical meaning remains UNKNOWN and is not used as a condition.
intent.unit_reason: One coherent identification-and-incidence task, with a complete solid/count description rather than separate clicks for counts. Minimum face count and the special spatial-diagonal definition must both be considered.
limitations: Selection recognizes a supplied name and incidence counts; it does not demonstrate independent naming or writing a minimum-face proof.
Historical circle-marker meaning remains UNKNOWN; source-glyph and source all-ink HOLDs are not resolved by this item.

rationales.derivation: A tetrahedron has three edges from an apex to the base vertices. If all non-base connections are incorrectly called diagonals, this produces three. They are edges, and their endpoints share faces; the correct spatial-diagonal count is zero.
rationales.misconception: Treat each of the three apex-to-base edges as a diagonal merely because it is not a base edge.

rationales.derivation: The face-neighbor lower bound is four and a tetrahedron attains it. Its four vertices have six pairwise edges; every vertex pair shares a triangular face, so there are zero spatial diagonals.
Counting the three edges of each of four triangular faces gives 4 times 3=12 face-edge incidences. Every edge belongs to two faces, so this must be divided by two to get six edges.
rationales.misconception: Count face-edge incidences as distinct edges, omitting the division by two.

rationales.derivation: A triangular prism has nine edges, six vertices and no spatial diagonals: nonadjacent pairs share a lateral face. Counting only its three lateral faces, however, wrongly makes it seem to beat a tetrahedron. Including its two triangular bases gives five faces, not the minimum four.
rationales.misconception: Minimize using only lateral faces and omit the two closing triangular faces of a prism.

view.stem: 一个凸多面体恰有五个面。判断四边形或五边形能否成为它的一个面，选出所有成立的存在性命题。

options.text: 存在一个有四边形面的五面体。
存在一个有五边形面的五面体。

intent.task: Settle each of the two face-existence questions, using an attaining construction for the quadrilateral and a face-adjacency obstruction for the pentagon.
intent.source_solution: A convex quadrilateral pyramid has one quadrilateral base and four triangular lateral faces, so it is a five-face witness. Each edge of a pentagonal face needs a different neighboring face: distinct sides cannot both be the intersection with the same supporting plane. Five neighbors plus the pentagonal face would require at least six faces. Quadrilateral is possible, pentagon is not.
intent.unit_reason: The shared five-face constraint makes this one multiple-selection task. The two mathematical existence assertions are judged separately, not encoded as a pair-combination choice or split into per-subpart yes/no questions.
limitations: Choice records existence judgments, not independent production of the example and impossibility argument.

rationales.derivation: Take a convex quadrilateral and one apex outside its plane. Its convex pyramid boundary has the quadrilateral and four triangular faces, for 1+4=5 faces.

A pentagonal pyramid has five lateral faces, but its pentagonal base adds a sixth face. More generally a pentagonal face needs five distinct neighboring faces, so any convex polyhedron containing it has at least six faces.
rationales.misconception: Use a pentagonal pyramid as a five-face example by counting its five lateral faces but omitting the base.

view.stem: 一个凸多面体的一个面是六边形。这个多面体最少有多少条棱？

intent.task: Prove an edge lower bound from one hexagonal face and exhibit a convex polyhedron attaining it.
intent.source_solution: The hexagonal face has six boundary edges and six vertices. At least three edges meet at each vertex of a nondegenerate convex solid, so each base vertex needs an edge leaving its supporting face plane. These are six distinct edges: an edge joining two base vertices would remain in that plane, not leave it, and a face diagonal is not an edge. Hence at least 6+6=12 edges. A hexagonal pyramid has exactly six base plus six apex edges, attaining twelve.
intent.unit_reason: One extremal task combines the local incidence lower bound with attainability. It is not six separate vertex-count clicks or a request to count a supplied diagram.
limitations: Selecting the minimum does not demonstrate independent writing of the lower bound or of the attaining construction.

rationales.derivation: The chosen hexagon has six sides. Stopping there counts only the face boundary and leaves each of its vertices with just two incident edges, insufficient for a closed three-dimensional convex polyhedron.
rationales.misconception: Count only the six edges of the given face and omit all edges leaving its plane.

rationales.derivation: Start with six base edges and one extra-edge incidence at each of six base vertices. Incorrectly halve the six extra incidences, producing 6+6/2=9. An extra edge has only one endpoint in the base face, so these six incidences are not paired within that list.
rationales.misconception: Apply division by two to a list containing only the base endpoints of the six non-base edges.

rationales.derivation: Six boundary edges plus at least one distinct edge leaving each of six base vertices gives twelve. A hexagonal pyramid has exactly these twelve edges, proving the bound is attained.
A hexagonal prism has six lower, six upper and six connecting edges, total eighteen. It is an example but not a minimum: the permitted hexagonal pyramid has twelve.
rationales.misconception: Assume that a hexagonal face forces a second congruent face and a prism, rather than minimizing across all allowed solids.

view.stem: 要作一个有8条棱的凸多面体，以下哪种构造满足要求？棱只计外表面各面的边，不计面内的对角线。

options.text: 取一个凸四边形和一个不在其平面内的顶点，作以该四边形为底的棱锥。
取一个凸五边形和一个不在其平面内的顶点，作以该五边形为底的棱锥。
把一个三角形平移到另一平行平面，连接对应顶点，作三棱柱。
在正方形中心的法线两侧各取一点，与四个顶点一起取凸包，作双棱锥。

intent.task: Preserve the request to construct an eight-edge solid by identifying a full geometrically valid construction specification and checking its edge incidence.
intent.source_solution: For eight edges, choose a convex quadrilateral in a plane and an apex outside it, then include its base and four triangular lateral faces. Four base plus four apex edges gives eight. For the source's separate nine-edge construction, a triangle and its translated copy with corresponding vertices joined form a prism with 3+3+3=9 edges. A triangular bipyramid is another nine-edge witness; its two apices must be on opposite sides with their connecting line through the triangle interior. These are independent textual constructions, not actual drawings.
intent.unit_reason: The eight-edge and nine-edge constructions are independent existence problems with different target incidence counts. This item checks the eight-edge construction as a complete solid, while a separate multiple item checks the nine-edge constructions; neither splits individual edges into clicks.
limitations: Original task says to construct a polyhedron. Choice recognizes a supplied construction and cannot reproduce or certify the learner's actual drawing, model building or independent construction design.
No new diagram is created; the actual eight-edge construction remains unperformed by this choice artifact.

rationales.derivation: A quadrilateral pyramid has its four base sides plus four apex-to-base edges, total 4+4=8. The off-plane apex guarantees a nondegenerate three-dimensional convex solid.

A pentagonal pyramid has five base edges and five apex edges, total ten. Counting all five base edges but only three front-facing apex edges would produce 5+3=8; hidden edges still belong to the solid.
rationales.misconception: Count only three visible apex edges of a pentagonal pyramid and omit the other two.

rationales.derivation: The translated triangles give 3+3=6 edges, and all three corresponding vertex pairs require connectors, giving nine. Dropping one connector gives the mistaken 6+2=8 and no longer counts the specified prism completely.
rationales.misconception: Include just two of the three corresponding-vertex connectors in a triangular prism.

rationales.derivation: The square bipyramid has four equatorial edges and four edges to each apex: 4+4+4=12. Counting only the eight apex edges omits all four equatorial edges, which remain edges between adjacent exterior triangular faces.
rationales.misconception: Discard the square's perimeter edges when gluing two pyramids, as if an internal equatorial face made its exterior boundary edges disappear.

view.stem: 要作一个有9条棱的凸多面体，选出所有满足要求的构造。棱只计外表面各面的边，不计面内的对角线。

options.text: 把一个三角形平移到另一平行平面，连接对应顶点，作三棱柱。
在三角形两侧各取一个顶点，使它们的连线穿过三角形内部，作这五点的凸包。
取一个凸四边形和一个不在其平面内的顶点，作以该四边形为底的棱锥。
取一个凸六边形和一个不在其平面内的顶点，作以该六边形为底的棱锥。

intent.task: Determine which complete construction specifications produce a convex nine-edge solid, retaining existence and edge-count reasoning rather than copying a drawing's visible lines.
intent.source_solution: The source requires an eight-edge and a nine-edge construction. A quadrilateral pyramid provides eight (4 base plus 4 apex edges). For nine, the convex prism obtained by translating a triangle has six triangle edges and three connectors. A convex triangular bipyramid also has nine: three equatorial edges and six edges to the two apices. The line-through-interior condition ensures the equatorial triangle is internal and all six lateral triangles are exterior faces. This supplies alternative independently derived nine-edge constructions, without drawing either.
intent.unit_reason: Nine-edge existence is mathematically independent of the eight-edge target. Multiple mode permits both genuine nine-edge constructions; it does not force a unique witness or use a coded combination of solids.
limitations: Recognition and incidence counting do not demonstrate that a learner can draw, build or independently devise a nine-edge polyhedron.
Actual construction/drawing requested in the source is not completed or certified.

rationales.derivation: The two triangular faces each have three edges; joining the three corresponding vertex pairs gives three more. Total 3+3+3=9, and the translated-triangle prism is convex.

Three equatorial edges plus three edges from each of two apices gives 3+3+3=9. With the apices on opposite sides and their line through the triangle interior, their convex hull is a nondegenerate triangular bipyramid, not two separated solids.

Four quadrilateral sides plus four apex connections gives eight. Adding one drawn diagonal of the quadrilateral gives the mistaken ninth line, but a face diagonal is not a boundary edge of this polyhedron.
rationales.misconception: Add one quadrilateral face diagonal to the eight genuine edges and count it as a ninth edge.

rationales.derivation: A hexagonal pyramid has six base and six apex edges, total twelve. Counting only three visible apex connections produces 6+3=9, but visibility cannot delete the other three edges.
rationales.misconception: Count all six base edges but only three front-facing apex edges of a hexagonal pyramid.

view.stem: 若一个集合中任意两点间的整条线段都属于该集合，就称它为凸集。判断下列关于凸多面体的命题，选出所有正确命题；每个命题都保留其中“所得集合是多面体”的条件。

options.text: 如果两个凸多面体的交集是多面体，那么这个多面体是凸的。
如果两个凸多面体的并集是多面体，那么这个多面体是凸的。

intent.task: Judge both original universally quantified propositions, distinguishing intersection's preservation of segment containment from union's failure even when the result is a polyhedron.
intent.source_solution: For x,y in P intersection Q, both endpoints belong to both convex sets. Thus every point on [x,y] is in both, hence in the intersection; the first proposition is true. For the union use the convex boxes P=[0,2]x[0,1]x[0,1] and Q=[0,1]x[0,2]x[0,1]. Their union is a closed L-shaped polyhedral prism. The points (2,1,1/2) and (1,2,1/2) belong to the union, but their midpoint (3/2,3/2,1/2) belongs to neither. Hence the second proposition is false. The first hypothesis already excludes intersections that are only points, segments or planar faces. Segment convexity is explicitly stated in the view; block 18 supplies the convex-study scope, not a falsely attributed missing formal definition.
intent.unit_reason: One multiple item judges the two substantive universal claims separately under their original hypotheses. Keeping both in a shared set-operation task tests the quantifier difference without combination codes or a series of trivial membership clicks.
limitations: A correct selected set records judgments, not the learner's independent segment proof or production and verification of the L-prism counterexample.
No choicePASS claim is a proof-completion claim; the proof and counterexample above are author reasoning only.

rationales.derivation: For any two intersection points, convexity puts their segment in each input polyhedron. All segment points therefore satisfy both memberships and belong to the intersection, so the result is convex.

Union endpoints need not lie in a common input polyhedron. In the two boxes P=[0,2]x[0,1]x[0,1], Q=[0,1]x[0,2]x[0,1], the endpoint pair (2,1,1/2),(1,2,1/2) has midpoint (3/2,3/2,1/2) outside both. Their union is nonetheless a polyhedron, so this is a counterexample under the exact hypothesis.
rationales.misconception: From each endpoint belonging to at least one input, incorrectly infer that both endpoints share a single convex input, then apply segment containment there.

view.stem: 图示多面体 $ABCDFE$ 的面 $ABCD$ 是边长为 $a$ 的正方形；面 $ABEF$ 是梯形，$|BE|=|EF|=|FA|=\frac{a}{2}$；$(ABE)\perp(ABC)$。设 $\alpha$ 为棱 $AF$ 对平面 $ABC$ 的倾斜角，$\theta$ 为平面 $ABC$ 和 $CDF$ 所成的角，$S$ 为展开图的面积。哪一项给出了这三个量的正确结果？

options.text: $\alpha=30^\circ$，$\theta=\arctan\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$，$S=\frac{3a^2}{16}(8+\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{19})$。
$\alpha=60^\circ$，$\theta=60^\circ$，$S=\frac{3a^2}{16}(8+\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{19})$。
$\alpha=60^\circ$，$\theta=\arctan\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$，$S=\frac{a^2}{16}(16+3\sqrt{3}+3\sqrt{19})$。
$\alpha=60^\circ$，$\theta=\arctan\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}$，$S=\frac{3a^2}{16}(8+\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{19})$。

intent.task: Retain all three requested computations using the existing solid: line-to-plane inclination, plane-to-plane inclination and the full area of a net.
intent.source_solution: Use cyclic face ABEF with parallel bases AB=a and EF=a/2 and equal legs a/2. Its two base offsets are a/4 and its perpendicular height h=sqrt((a/2)^2-(a/4)^2)=sqrt(3)a/4. Set A=(0,0,0),B=(a,0,0),D=(0,a,0),C=(a,a,0),F=(a/4,0,h),E=(3a/4,0,h). Then tan(alpha)=h/(a/4)=sqrt(3), so alpha=60 degrees. ABC and CDF intersect along CD; a perpendicular cross-section has horizontal span a and vertical rise h, giving tan(theta)=sqrt(3)/4, equivalently cos(theta)=4/sqrt(19). The five boundary faces are ABCD,ABEF,ADF,BCE,CDEF. Their areas are respectively a^2,3sqrt(3)a^2/16,a^2/4,a^2/4,3sqrt(19)a^2/16, since CDEF's slant height is sqrt(a^2+h^2)=sqrt(19)a/4. Their sum is S=3a^2(8+sqrt(3)+sqrt(19))/16. A cut net preserves face areas; no net drawing is needed for this area computation and none is produced.
intent.unit_reason: One complete triple keeps the three coupled computations and the shared geometry together. Distractors come from three independent geometric errors, so solving only one subpart does not distinguish all options. No answer-slot conversion or cellwise arithmetic clicks are used.
limitations: Choice recognizes final derived quantities; it does not prove the learner independently wrote the projection, perpendicular cross-section or five-face area derivation.
The original third task asks for net area, not to draw a net. No actual net drawing or general drawing ability is certified.
No new diagram, source-wide all-ink approval, exact-label recovery, product-width measurement or image semantic-review pass is claimed.

Exactly two image loads total, zero reopens/crops.

rationales.derivation: The perpendicular height is sqrt(3)a/4 and AF's in-plane projection is a/4. Reversing these legs gives tan(alpha)=(a/4)/(sqrt(3)a/4)=1/sqrt(3), yielding 30 degrees instead of 60. The plane angle and area here remain the independently derived correct values.
rationales.misconception: Interchange the vertical height and horizontal projection when taking the line-to-plane tangent, thereby computing the complementary angle.

rationales.derivation: The plane-angle cross-section perpendicular to CD spans the full square width a. Reusing the trapezoid's short side offset a/4 instead gives tan(theta)=h/(a/4)=sqrt(3), yielding 60 degrees. The correct theta is arctan(sqrt(3)/4); alpha and area remain correct.
rationales.misconception: Reuse AF's a/4 projection as the plane-angle horizontal span, instead of the distance a between CD and the line AB.

rationales.derivation: Retaining only the square and the two trapezoids gives a^2+3sqrt(3)a^2/16+3sqrt(19)a^2/16 = a^2(16+3sqrt(3)+3sqrt(19))/16. The two triangular faces ADF and BCE each add a^2/4, so the displayed area is missing a^2/2. Both displayed angles are correct.
rationales.misconception: Omit both triangular end faces when summing the area of the net, treating the three quadrilateral faces as the complete surface.

rationales.derivation: Offsets a/4 and height sqrt(3)a/4 give alpha=60 degrees. A CD-perpendicular cross-section has span a, giving theta=arctan(sqrt(3)/4). Summing the square, two trapezoids and two triangles yields a^2+a^2/2+3a^2(sqrt(3)+sqrt(19))/16 = 3a^2(8+sqrt(3)+sqrt(19))/16.
